A Little Goes a Long Way

No shelter. No rent. Just care.

Our animals live with foster families instead of in a building, so donations don't go to rent or kennels. They go to what animals actually need:

  • Vet exams and vaccines
  • Spay and neuter surgeries
  • Microchips
  • Food and supplies for foster homes

How Community Fostering Works

Most of our animals come to us through a neighbor who stopped to help.

  1. 1
    A neighbor finds an animal

    A stray cat under a porch, a dog loose on the street. They reach out and ask what to do.

  2. 2
    They foster, we cover the rest

    We pay for vet care and handle the marketing. There are no upfront costs for the foster.

  3. 3
    The animal goes home

    We review applications and help match the animal with the right adopter.

Learn about fostering

Beyond Adoption

Helping every kind of animal

We work toward a community full of healthy and happy animals, regardless of species or domestication.

  • Wildlife. Advice on living alongside coyotes, possums and birds, and who to call when one is hurt.
  • Lost or hurt animals. Clear next steps for anyone who finds an animal in trouble.
  • Community cats. Support for neighbors caring for outdoor cats.
  • Free and low-cost pet care. A guide to affordable vets, food and supplies.
  • Independent rescuers. A place to list their animals, find fosters and borrow equipment.

The Stories Behind the Numbers

Success Story: Pepper

Pepper came to us as a nervous stray puppy and spent four months with a foster family learning to trust people.

She's been home with her family for a year now. She's one of more than 400, and every one started with a neighbor who opened their home.
